newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moskvich carmaker seen working with Moscow, Renault.
newsitem.headline: Moskvich carmaker seen working with Moscow, Renault.

text.p: Russian carmaker AO Moskvich and France's Renault are holding talks in Moscow as Russia plans to transfer control of the factory to the Moscow city government, the company's chief administrator said on Wednesday.

"There is no agreement but talks are in progress and a group of specialists from Renault is now at the factory," said Yevgeny Gassan, chief of administration at Moskvich, which used to produce the Moskvich sedan but was shut for most of 1996.
Gassan said that a presidential order being prepared would effectively stop plans to sell 49 percent of the company to private investors and give the company to Moscow city.

"A presidential decree has been prepared transferring the federal shares packet to Moscow and has passed practically all stages of review. Monday it went to the presidential adminsitration and now we wait," he said.
Gassan said that the Moscow city government would probably receive the federal government's 60 percent share of the factory and that 2.3 trillion roubles in debts would be rescheduled.
"According to the decree, if Moscow pays all current debts, the old debts can be put off."
The move would stop or delay plans to sell 33 percent of Moskvich in an investment tender. Altogether it had been planned to sell 49 percent of the company.
"That was the plan, but now we don't know," he said.
He said Moskvich had resumed limited operations but had not yet produced a single car and would be forced to stop without further funds, expected from the Moscow government.
"We expected to produce 1,000 cars in January, but it's already February and we have not produced anything. So far we hvaen't received financial support from anyone," he said.
